findings.evidence: `grep -n 'relabel_id\|relabel_relabel\|relabel_comp' EpsilonEridani/Particles/Parton/` returns no hits; the only relabel lemmas are `relabel_apply`, `mellinMoment_relabel`, `sum_mellinMoment_relabel`, `*.relabel`, `relabel_valenceTarget` (Basic.lean:160-206). Species.lean:170-172 proves `chargeConj_chargeConj` by `ext s x Q2; simp`, which is exactly the symptom of the missing composition law.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma relabel_id (f : Pdf ι) : relabel id f = f` and `@[simp] lemma relabel_relabel (σ : κ → ι) (τ : μ → κ) (f : Pdf ι) : relabel τ (relabel σ f) = relabel (σ ∘ τ) f`, and derive `chargeConj_chargeConj` from the latter plus `conj_conj` instead of `ext s x Q2; simp`.
findings.issue: `relabel` is newly exposed general infrastructure (the PR states "Charge conjugation, and later the isospin and flavour relabellings, are instances"), but its characteristic API stops at `relabel_apply`: there is no `relabel_id` (`relabel id f = f`) and no composition law (`relabel σ (relabel τ f) = relabel (τ ∘ σ) f`). A consumer composing two relabellings must drop to `ext` + `relabel_apply` every time.

findings.evidence: `SumRuleAssumptions.valence : ∀ i Q2, mellinMoment f 0 i Q2 = valenceTarget i` (Basic.lean:133) and `valenceNumber` is literally the difference of two `mellinMoment f 0` values (Species.lean:225-226); no lemma connects them — `grep valenceTarget EpsilonEridani/` shows only `chargeConj_valenceTarget` and `relabel_valenceTarget`.
findings.fix: Add `theorem valenceNumber_eq_sub_valenceTarget [Fintype Flavor] {f : Pdf (Species Flavor)} (h : SumRuleAssumptions f) (i : Flavor) (Q2 : ℝ) : valenceNumber f i Q2 = h.valenceTarget (.quark i) - h.valenceTarget (.antiquark i)`, proved by `rw [valenceNumber_def, h.valence, h.valence]`.
findings.issue: `valenceNumber` has no interaction lemma with `SumRuleAssumptions`, the operation in scope and the stated consumer. The PR says §1.2 is "a meson-level predicate equating `PDF.valenceNumber f i Q2` with the meson's net valence numbers ... against `PDF.SumRuleAssumptions`", but to do that a consumer must unfold via `valenceNumber_def` and apply `valence_sumRule` twice by hand.

findings.evidence: Species.lean:238-242 states the lemma only for `f (.quark i) = f (.antiquark i)`; the docstring at 238-239 claims it "applies to every flavour of a density invariant under charge conjugation", but no declaration in the file takes `chargeConj f = f` as a hypothesis (`grep -n 'chargeConj f = f' Species.lean` → no hits).
findings.fix: Add `theorem valenceNumber_eq_zero_of_chargeConj_eq {f : Pdf (Species Flavor)} (h : chargeConj f = f) (i : Flavor) (Q2 : ℝ) : valenceNumber f i Q2 = 0`, derived from `valenceNumber_chargeConj` and `h` (`x = -x → x = 0`).
findings.issue: `valenceNumber_eq_zero_of_eq` takes the pointwise hypothesis `f (.quark i) = f (.antiquark i)`, and its docstring advertises the C-invariant application, but the corollary for the actual hypothesis a consumer holds — `chargeConj f = f` — is absent. Roadmap §1.3 names precisely this case ("the neutral pion's own charge-conjugation symmetry be derived").

summary: The surface is minimal and free of compatibility artefacts, and the bundled definitions carry no free data. But three characteristic lemmas are missing: `relabel` has no identity/composition law, and `valenceNumber` has no interaction lemma with either `SumRuleAssumptions` or charge-conjugation invariance — the two things the PR description names as its purpose.
